text: When setting project goals, it is essential to make them SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. This clarity helps teams understand exactly what needs to be done and by when. Next, break the main goal into smaller milestones. These checkpoints allow you to track progress and stay motivated, as each completed phase brings you closer to the final result. Also, clearly define your deliverables—the tangible outputs you will produce, such as reports or prototypes. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment. Discuss the goals with everyone involved early on to confirm that their expectations match your plan. This reduces confusion and builds a strong foundation for a successful project.
